exposure: Delivery mode (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: 103,174 Taiwanese women who delivered babies between January 1, 2000, and December 31, 2018
finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with an increased risk of stress urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse compared to cesarean section.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with an increased risk of stress urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse compared to cesarean section.
